problem: Given the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.

activity_context.topic_title: Tangent Vectors and Tangent Lines to Curves

examples.knowledge_point: Finding Points Where a Tangent Vector is Perpendicular to Another Vector
examples.problem: Given the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle t^2+1\,,\, 6t+3\right\rangle,$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $\left\langle 3\,,\, 1\right\rangle.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $\mathbf r(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1)\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t\,,\,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $\left\langle 3\,,\, 1 \right\rangle$ and $\mathbf r'(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $\left\langle 3\,,\, 1 \right\rangle \cdot \mathbf r'(t) = 0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨3\,,\,1⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨3\,,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨2t\,,\,6⟩ & =0 \\ 3\cdot 2t+1\cdot 6 & =0 \\ 6t+6 & =0 \\ t & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only solution is $t=-1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨(-1)^{2}+1\,,\,6(-1)+3⟩=⟨2\,,\,-3⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $\left\langle 3\,,\, 1\right\rangle$ and $\mathbf r'(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(2,-3).$

feedback.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)={e}^{t}\,i+3t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k$ at the point corresponding to $t=\pi ,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
feedback.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=\pi $,  the vector ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
R(u)=r(\pi )+u{r}^{′}(\pi ),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi ) & ={e}^{\pi }\,i+3(\pi )\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2(\pi )\,k \\  & ={e}^{\pi }\,i+3\pi \,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,k \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+3\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi ) & ={e}^{(\pi )}\,i+3\,j+\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡2(\pi )k \\  & ={e}^{\pi }\,i+3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point 
 where $t=\pi $ is 

$$
R(u)={e}^{\pi }\,i+3\pi \,j+\,k+u({e}^{\pi }\,i+3\,j),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
